final_note: By the end of Chapter 7, Kestrel is no longer simply accompanying the anomaly—she is part of the line that keeps things from breaking, choosing presence, restraint, and deliberate trust in a world that rewards neither.
final_note_addendum_ch11: By the end of Chapter 11, Kestrel’s restraint evolves into administrative combat: she learns to treat wards, labels, and quiet-hours procedure as terrain. When Irix is harmed and fear turns inward, Kestrel becomes the stabilizing hinge—protecting dignity, preventing escalation that would become institutional ammunition, and turning chaos into a reportable timeline.
final_note_addendum_ch12: By the end of Chapter 12, Kestrel’s role hardens into explicit guardianship for Irix while her bond with Jayson strengthens through boundary-respect and repair. She proves she can hold procedure and tenderness at once: reportcraft in one hand, dinner-routine stability in the other, refusing to let cruelty or rumor turn their trio into easy prey.
